title: Cyber defamation - how it differs from regular defamation
p1:
A single post online can damage a reputation faster than years of hard work can build it.

But did you know cyber defamation is not just “regular defamation on the internet”?
p2: Many people think the only difference is the platform used. The bigger difference is the speed, reach, and permanence of online content. A false statement shared on social media can spread to thousands of people within minutes and may continue affecting someone even after it is deleted.
p3: Regular defamation usually involves harmful false statements shared through traditional methods like speech or print. Cyber defamation involves digital spaces such as social media, websites, emails, or online forums. The key lesson: before sharing accusations or claims online, verify the facts. A quick post can create long-lasting consequences for both the person targeted and the person posting it.
conclusion: Have you ever seen an online post that damaged someone's reputation before the facts were verified?
